title: The Köppen Climate Map
objective: After this level you can explain how climates are classified by temperature and rainfall and read a place's climate type.
summary: Köppen's first letter sorts climates by temperature, except dry B. Later letters add rainfall and heat, so Cs, the Mediterranean climate, means mild with a dry summer.

cards.headline: Southern California and the Mediterranean coast share one climate code: Cs.
cards.body: Two letters, and a climate scientist can picture the summers and the winters. You met Köppen's five climate groups in World Geography. Now learn to read the code itself.

cards.headline: First letter: how warm?
cards.body: The first letter sorts by temperature, with one exception. A tropical climate (A) has no month cooler than 18 °C. A polar climate (E) has no month warmer than 10 °C. C and D are midlatitude climates in between, also set by temperature. The odd one out is B: dry climates are defined by dryness, not heat. So a desert can be scorching or freezing and still be a B.

cards.headline: Next letters: when does it rain?
cards.body: The second letter tracks rainfall through the year: f means no dry season, s means a dry summer, and w means a dry winter. In the B group it's different: W marks a true desert and S a semiarid steppe. A third letter can add heat: h for hot, k for cold. So BWh is a hot desert, and BWk is a cold one.

cards.headline: Reading Cs
cards.body: Put it together. C means a mild midlatitude climate, and s means the summer is the dry season. That's the Mediterranean climate: hot, dry summers and cool, wet winters. It sits between about 30° and 45° latitude on the western sides of continents, which is how southern California ends up sharing a code with the Mediterranean coast.
cards.callout: A, C, D, E: temperature · B: dryness · f / s / w: when the dry season falls

cards.headline: Climate codes: cracked
learned: A, C, D and E are set by temperature
f, s and w say when the dry season falls

questions.prompt: In a Köppen code such as Cs, what does the second letter s tell you?

options.label: The place has no dry season
The place is a semiarid steppe
options.rationale: That's S, used in the dry B group.

questions.explanation: In Köppen codes, s marks a dry summer, as in the Mediterranean climate, Cs.

questions.prompt: How can a scorching desert and a freezing desert both end up in Köppen's group B?

options.label: Group B is defined by dryness, not temperature
Both have a warmest month below 10 °C
options.rationale: That's the rule for polar E climates.

options.label: Both have a coolest month of 18 °C or more
options.rationale: That's the rule for tropical A climates.

options.label: Group B is for any place with extreme weather
options.rationale: The B rule is about dryness.

questions.explanation: A, C, D and E are sorted by temperature, but B is set by dryness, so hot and cold deserts share it.

questions.prompt: Two hills weather from the same granite, but one sits in an A climate and the other in an E climate. Using Level 9, why will their soils differ?

options.label: They won't: the same rock always gives the same soil
options.rationale: Level 9 lists five soil-forming factors, not one.

options.label: Köppen letters are drawn from soil maps
options.rationale: They come from temperature and rainfall.

options.label: Climate is one of the five factors that shape soil
Only living things can change a soil
options.rationale: Living things are one factor of five.

questions.explanation: Soil depends on parent material, climate, living things, topography and time. Change the climate and you get a different soil.
